after_release.caveat: The after-release sample follows variant-dependent attachment SHA256 hashing and metadata/packet receipt construction. Baseline additionally hashes the avoided font copies. This sample is not an isolated production close/teardown comparison, so lower after-release footprint must not be claimed as production post-close savings. Weak probes substantiate reader destruction; process counters alone do not establish why allocator/VM memory remains.

audit_kind: independent retrospective audit of existing native evidence
limitations: Single virtual Apple M1 host with macOS 26.6.2 and the archived compiler/FFmpeg versions; no cross-device or cross-version replication.
Font-labeled payloads are synthetic repetitive bytes, not real renderable fonts. They test metadata admission and ownership, not rendered font fidelity.
The six-pair timing distributions are inconsistent and have outliers; no general opening-time speedup is established.
The benchmark retains complete production input classes but is not a full interactive MediaSession, PiP, or sustained playback workload.
Historical frame-step performance and timestamp-discovery fixtures were absent; ten tests per configuration explicitly skipped, including one older mixed-attachment fixture test.
The observed retained RSS/physical-footprint regression is verified; its allocator or VM mechanism is not established by these counters.
After-release work differs by variant and cannot support a clean production teardown-memory claim.

method.before_adjustment: For each pair and metric: (candidate retained - candidate before) - (baseline retained - baseline before).
method.inputs: Existing JSON observations, fixture manifests, parity receipts, archived native-test logs and git show of the exact manifest commits. No production sources, GitHub objects, or benchmark processes were changed or run.
method.memory_units: All stored memory values are bytes. Divide by 1048576 for MiB.
method.ordering: Checked exact sequence 0..227; six pairs; baseline/candidate order reverses each pair and scenario order reverses on odd pairs.
method.receipts: Checked every reader role, index, inclusion flag, count, exact copied bytes and attachment filenames/MIME/sizes/SHA256 against the fixture manifest; compared all metadata, codec-private and full packet traces to the common parity receipts.
method.sign_convention: Memory audit differences are candidate minus baseline; positive means higher memory usage. Reproduced copied-font and timing summaries retain the original baseline-minus-candidate reduction convention.
method.source_checks: SHA256 of exact bytes returned by git show <manifest commit>:<source path>, compared with every archived source hash and the three driver/harness/generator hashes.
method.summary: Independently recomputed each original metric median/min/max, six paired baseline-minus-candidate reductions and paired percentage reductions, then required exact equality with the entire saved summary.
method.test_counts: Counts of passed test-function lines and explicit skipped-test lines were independently read from each archived compressed test log; framework summary includes skips.

recommendation.rationale: The optimization removes unused owning Swift font copies and lowers malloc bytes in use, but retained resident memory and physical footprint increase in every heavy-fixture pair. Peak RSS does not improve and opening timings are inconsistent. Current evidence does not establish successful memory-performance optimization. Preserve this research; do not present allocation ownership reductions as process-memory savings.
